title: Sum of the Smallest Number of Every Stretch
statement: Look at every **non-empty contiguous stretch** of `numbers`. For each stretch take its **smallest number**. Return the **sum** of these smallest numbers over all stretches, **modulo 1,000,000,007** (the sum can be very large).

hints.nudge: Instead of looking at each stretch, ask for each NUMBER: in how many stretches is it the smallest?
hints.pattern: Monotonic stack: for each position find how far the stretch may extend to the left and to the right while the number stays the minimum; the number contributes value * leftChoices * rightChoices.
hints.pseudocode:
left[i] = i - (position of the previous number that is <= numbers[i], or -1)
right[i] = (position of the next number that is < numbers[i], or n) - i
answer = sum of numbers[i] * left[i] * right[i], modulo 1,000,000,007
hints.walkthrough: There are n(n + 1)/2 stretches, so computing each minimum separately is O(n^2) at best. Count per number instead. A stretch has numbers[i] as its minimum if it contains i and does not contain a smaller number. Going left from i you can extend until the previous smaller (or equal) number; going right until the next strictly smaller number: left[i] and right[i] choices for the two ends, so numbers[i] is the minimum of left[i] * right[i] stretches. To avoid counting a stretch with two equal minimums twice, one side stops at equal numbers and the other does not (above: left stops at <=, right at <). Both boundary arrays come from one monotonic-stack pass each. The products need 64-bit numbers (30000 * 30000 * 30000 is about 2.7 * 10^13), reduced modulo 1,000,000,007.
